title: Replicating steering-strength/coherence tradeoff curves and finding the optimal layer per family

original_idea.body:
# Replicating steering-strength/coherence tradeoff curves and finding the optimal layer per family

**Problem:** Layer-14-best-for-Gemma and central-layer-best findings are scattered across papers. A unified replication that maps the steering-coefficient-vs-coherence tradeoff and best layer across three open families for one safety concept is a clean, beginner-friendly synthesis.

**Direction:** For a fixed refusal vector, sweep injection layer and coefficient on Gemma-2-2B, Qwen2.5-3B, and Llama-3.2-3B, plotting behavior-shift vs. coherence (perplexity) tradeoff curves and identifying the optimal operating point per family. Twist: a standardized cross-family tradeoff atlas.

**Why it matters:** A reusable map of where and how hard to steer each family lowers the barrier for all downstream safety-steering work and prevents practitioners from over-steering into incoherence. Pure analysis, single GPU, no lab resources.

**Relevant context:** Gemma layer-14 steerability; central-layer coherence-tradeoff findings (arXiv:2509.06608); Tan et al. reliability analysis.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (operating-range atlas aids safety steering) but indirect, a gap to catastrophic-risk reduction.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Layer/coefficient sweep with perplexity metric on small models, standard tools, beginner makes progress.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused sweep producing tradeoff curves; clear methodology but three families adds breadth.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Mixed: useful reusable infrastructure but layer/coefficient sweeps are commonly run.

low_compute.reasoning: Pure inference on 2-3B models, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Layer/coefficient coherence tradeoffs are largely studied; this is mostly synthesis.
